title: Empirical Verification of Aqueous Specific Heat Capacity via Continuous Heating
author: Dr. Sarah Lin, MOSEB Physical Chemistry Unit
abstract: We investigated the heat capacity of 150.0 mL pure deionized water under continuous thermal input from an atmospheric burner. The initial temperature of 21.2°C rose to a final steady boiling plateau at 99.8°C. Measured enthalpy absorption yielded c = 4.179 J/g·°C, exhibiting a 0.12% relative error from literature.
hypothesis: Under constant burner flame flux, liquid water will demonstrate linear sensible heating proportional to reciprocal mass until boiling point vaporization is reached.
methodology: Transferred 150 mL DI water into a 250 mL borosilicate beaker equipped with an immersion thermocouple. Bunsen burner ignited with constant blue flame. Recorded temperature and volume at 5-second intervals.
observations: Small convective nucleation bubbles formed at 68°C. Vigorous rolling boiling observed at 99.8°C with minor vaporization loss of 2.1 mL.
conclusion: The empirical sensible heat capacity of liquid water matches established IUPAC thermochemical constants within experimental uncertainty bounds.
